workflowUi.stereoHelp: Keeps left and right apart. If your voice is only in one ear, choose a mono option.

workflowUi.title: Title

levelEditor.hint: Every 6 dB doubles or halves the level. Watch the result stay left of 0 dBFS to avoid clipping.
levelEditor.graph: A typical voice at {{input}} dBFS comes out at {{output}} dBFS
levelEditor.graphSilent: A typical voice at {{input}} dBFS is silent at the output

bassTreble.bassDb: Boosts or cuts voice warmth and the low end. 0 dB leaves it unchanged.
bassTreble.trebleDb: Boosts or cuts voice brightness and articulation. 0 dB leaves it unchanged.
bassTreble.bassFrequencyHz: Raise this frequency to affect more of your voice. Default: 500 Hz. Original tuning: 120 Hz.
bassTreble.trebleFrequencyHz: Lower this frequency to affect more of your voice. Default: 1500 Hz. Original tuning: 6000 Hz.

testSignal.frequencyHz: Pitch of the test tone. 440 Hz is the A above middle C.
testSignal.levelDb: Loudness of the tone; 0 dBFS is the loudest possible. Start low, for example −18 dBFS.
testSignal.durationMs: How long the tone plays each time you press its Play button.

mute.muted: Silences everything passing through this node.

compressor.thresholdDb: Sound louder than this is turned down, evening out loud and quiet moments.
compressor.ratio: How strongly sound above the threshold is reduced: at 4, 4 dB over the threshold comes out 1 dB over.
compressor.attackMs: How quickly compression starts when the sound gets loud.
compressor.releaseMs: How quickly compression lets go when the sound gets quieter.
compressor.kneeDb: Softens the change around the threshold. 0 dB is an abrupt change.
compressor.makeupDb: Adds level back after compression so the result is not quieter overall.

gate.thresholdDb: Sound quieter than this is turned down, for example background noise between words.
gate.rangeDb: How much quiet sound is turned down. 80 dB is nearly silent; lower values sound more natural.
gate.hysteresisDb: The gate closes only once the sound falls this far below the threshold, which prevents rapid on/off chatter.
gate.ratio: How steeply sound below the threshold is reduced. Higher values act more like an on/off switch.
gate.attackMs: How quickly the gate opens when you start speaking.
gate.holdMs: How long the gate stays open after the sound drops, so word endings are not cut off.
gate.releaseMs: How quickly the gate closes after the hold time.

limiter.ceilingDb: The loudest level allowed out. Peaks above it are held down so they never clip.
limiter.lookaheadMs: Delays the sound slightly so sudden peaks are caught before they happen.
limiter.releaseMs: How quickly the limiter stops reducing after a peak.

delay.delayMs: Holds the sound back by this time, for example to line audio up with video.

pitch.semitones: Shifts the pitch in musical steps; 12 semitones is one octave.
pitch.cents: Small pitch adjustment; 100 cents make one semitone.

dehum.frequencyHz: Base frequency of the hum: 50 Hz in most of Europe, Asia, Africa and Australia, 60 Hz in North America.
dehum.amountPercent: How strongly the hum is removed.
dehum.harmonics: How many multiples of the hum frequency (for example 100 Hz, 150 Hz) are also removed.

declick.thresholdPercent: How much a spike must stand out to count as a click. Lower values remove more clicks but can soften consonants.

denoise.reductionPercent: How strongly the learned noise is removed.
denoise.floorPercent: How much of the noise stays. 0 % removes all of it, which can sound unnatural.
denoise.learning: On while the tool measures the noise to remove. Use Learn noise above.

speechDenoise.strengthPercent: How strongly background noise around speech is reduced.

firFilter.wetPercent: How much filtered (“wet”) sound you hear. 100 % is only the filtered sound, 0 % only the original (“dry”) sound; values in between blend them.
firFilter.gainDb: Adjusts the level after filtering, for example to match the original loudness.

spectralGate.thresholdDb: How much louder than the learned noise a frequency must be to pass. Raise it if noise still comes through; lower it if your voice sounds thin.
spectralGate.reductionDb: How much blocked frequencies are turned down. 80 dB is nearly silent.
spectralGate.learning: On while the tool measures the noise. Use Learn noise above.

timeShift.bufferSeconds: How many seconds of recent audio are kept so you can jump back and replay them.

recorder.format: WAV 24-bit keeps full quality for editing; MP3 makes small files to share.
recorder.autoRecord: Every Play starts a new recording; Stop saves it.
recorder.splitMinutes: Start a new file after this many minutes so long sessions stay manageable. 0 keeps one file per take.

duck.keyNodeId: The source or tool whose level turns this audio down, usually your microphone or voice chain.
duck.thresholdDb: Ducking starts when the trigger is louder than this. Set it between your room noise and your voice.
duck.amountDb: How far this audio is turned down while the trigger is active. 6 dB is about half as loud.
duck.attackMs: How quickly the audio goes down when you start talking.
duck.holdMs: How long the audio stays down after the trigger falls, so short pauses between words do not pump.
duck.releaseMs: How quickly the audio comes back after the hold time.

funVoiceChanger.preset: A starting voice. Pick one, then adjust any setting below.
funVoiceChanger.gateDb: Sound quieter than this is muted before the effects, so room noise does not trigger them. −90 dB is off.
funVoiceChanger.correctEnabled: Pulls your voice to the nearest note of the chosen scale.
funVoiceChanger.key: The key of the scale your voice is pulled to.
funVoiceChanger.scale: Which notes are allowed. Chromatic allows every note; Monotone holds one note for a robot voice.
funVoiceChanger.retuneMs: How quickly a note is pulled into tune. 0 ms snaps instantly, the hard tuned-vocal sound.
funVoiceChanger.humanizePercent: Leaves held notes a little loose so long notes keep their natural movement.
funVoiceChanger.shiftEnabled: Moves your voice up or down and changes its size.
funVoiceChanger.pitchSemitones: How far the voice moves up or down, in semitones. 12 is one octave.
funVoiceChanger.pitchCents: Small pitch steps; 100 cents is one semitone.
funVoiceChanger.formantSemitones: The size of the voice without changing its note: lower sounds bigger, higher sounds smaller.
funVoiceChanger.ringEnabled: Multiplies the voice by a tone for metallic robot and alien sounds.
funVoiceChanger.ringHz: Low values buzz; high values sound bell-like and alien.
funVoiceChanger.ringDepthPercent: How much of the ring-modulated sound replaces the voice.
funVoiceChanger.crushEnabled: Lowers the audio quality on purpose for a lo-fi, digital sound.
funVoiceChanger.crushBits: Fewer bits add more grainy distortion. 16 is clean.
funVoiceChanger.crushDownsample: Holds each sample for longer, like a cheap old device. 1 is off.
funVoiceChanger.driveEnabled: Distorts the voice, from warm grit to a blown-out megaphone.
funVoiceChanger.drivePercent: How hard the voice is pushed into distortion.
funVoiceChanger.whisperPercent: Replaces the voiced tone with breath while keeping the words. 0 % is off.
funVoiceChanger.toneEnabled: Cuts lows and highs and adds a peak, for radio or phone sounds.
funVoiceChanger.peakHz: Where the tone peak boosts or cuts.
funVoiceChanger.peakDb: How much the peak frequency is boosted (positive) or cut (negative).
funVoiceChanger.modEnabled: Chorus doubles the voice; flanger adds a sweeping, jet-like sound.
funVoiceChanger.modFeedbackPercent: Flanger only: stronger, ringing sweeps. Negative inverts them.
funVoiceChanger.spaceEnabled: Adds a room or cave echo around the voice.
funVoiceChanger.spaceSizePercent: Small rooms sound close; large ones sound distant.
funVoiceChanger.spaceDecayMs: How long the echo takes to fade away.
funVoiceChanger.spaceLevelPercent: How loud the echo is next to the voice.
funVoiceChanger.mixPercent: 100 % is only the changed voice; lower values blend in your normal voice.
funVoiceChanger.outputDb: Level after the effects, to match your normal voice.

inputSwitch.selected: Which input you hear: A or B.
inputSwitch.fade: Normal changes over half a second; Slow fades over two seconds.

outputSwitch.selected: Which destination receives audio: A or B.

parameterUi.gainHelp: Makes the sound louder (positive) or quieter (negative). 0 dB leaves it unchanged.
parameterUi.volumeHelp: 100 % leaves the sound unchanged, 0 % silences it, 200 % doubles it.
parameterUi.bandHelp: Boosts or cuts the sound around {{frequency}}.

canvasUi.receiveHandle: Receive (end) - drag from the sending tool's blue dot to the receiving tool's orange dot.
canvasUi.active: Moving lights: audio is flowing. Colour, glow and number of lights follow the level (teal quiet, gold speech, orange loud, red near clipping)
canvasUi.configured: Solid grey: connected, session stopped or not metered
canvasUi.disabled: Orange dashes: connection paused, node disabled, or muted
canvasUi.unavailable: Yellow dots: source not connected yet (app closed or not started) or audio stale
canvasUi.faulted: Red dots: a plugin on this path failed
canvasUi.arrangeHint: Inputs on the left, outputs on the right, tools in between, with room around every connection
canvasUi.mapHint: Show a small map of the whole route

toolProperties.privacyMuted: Privacy mute is on: every microphone and captured app is silent, not only this tool.
toolProperties.privacyHint: Privacy mute silences every microphone and captured app right away.
toolProperties.rename: Click the name to rename this tool. Press Enter or click away to finish; Escape cancels.
toolProperties.autosave: Parameter edits save automatically after a short pause while audio plays. Other changes need Save at the top; the canvas marks tools that need saving.
toolProperties.timing: For delay and processing measurements, open Timing while audio plays. Ready means enabled for the next playback; Active does not guarantee an incoming signal.
toolProperties.flags: Off silences inputs and outputs; an off effect passes sound without processing. Bypass passes sound around an effect; on a prepared input, output, or Mixer it silences that contribution. Live toggles do not require Save or Stop and keep your other edits. Off devices remain open until Stop and contribute silence.
toolProperties.guideError: Could not open the guide. Visit {{url}}

toolShelf.step1: Add a source: Input Device, Test Signal, Audio File, or an application.
toolShelf.step2: Add processing tools such as Gain or Advanced EQ if needed.
toolShelf.step3: Add an Output Device and choose your speakers or headphones in Properties.
toolShelf.step4: Drag from the sending tool's blue dot to the receiving tool's orange dot.
toolShelf.step5: Press Play to hear it. Use Save at the top when the canvas marks changes that need saving.
toolShelf.pinHint: Pin a tool to keep it here
toolShelf.preview: Point at a tool to see what it does. Click to add it, or drag it onto the canvas.
toolShelf.empty: No built-in tools match your search. Try a name such as Gain or Recorder.
toolShelf.applicationHelp: Capture audio from a running app into this route.
toolShelf.groupHelp: A named visual background. It carries no audio.

physical-input.name: Input device
physical-input.help: Sound from a microphone, line input, or virtual cable (for example CABLE Output). Choose the device in Properties.

test-signal.name: Test Signal
test-signal.help: A steady tone for checking a route without speaking. Press Play tone on its card to start it.

audio-file.name: Audio file
audio-file.help: Play a WAV or MP3 through the graph. Select media in the node properties.

soundboard.name: Soundboard
soundboard.help: Up to nine sounds on buttons. Trigger them here, from the API or from a Stream Deck.

endpoint-loopback.name: Endpoint loopback
endpoint-loopback.help: Select an exact active render endpoint in Endpoint binding

virtual-render-source.name: Cable input
virtual-render-source.help: Sound that another app plays into an AudioRouter cable (for example a game set to output to Cable A Input). Choose the cable in Properties.

physical-output.name: Output device
physical-output.help: Send sound to speakers, headphones, or a virtual cable (for example CABLE Input) that another app uses as its input. Choose the device in Properties.

network-receive.name: Network Receive
network-receive.help: Play audio streamed by AudioRouter on another computer on your network, for example game audio from a gaming PC. Enter that computer's IP address.

network-send.name: Network Send
network-send.help: Stream audio to AudioRouter on another computer on your network, for example from a gaming PC to a streaming PC. Enter the receiving computer's IP address.

virtual-capture-sink.name: Cable output
virtual-capture-sink.help: Send sound into an AudioRouter cable that another app records from (for example Discord's microphone set to Cable B Output). Choose the cable in Properties.

volume.name: Volume
volume.help: Set one source's level in percent (0–200 %) before it reaches a Mixer.

gain.name: Gain
gain.help: Make the sound louder or quieter, in decibels.

bass-treble.name: Bass & Treble
bass-treble.help: Shape voice warmth and brightness by up to 12 dB. Adjustable shelf frequencies let you affect more or less of your voice.

dehum.name: Dehum
dehum.help: Remove low-frequency electrical hum at 50 or 60 Hz and its harmonics.

declick.name: Declick
declick.help: Repair clicks, pops, and crackle. A lower threshold repairs more but may alter sharp sounds.

denoise.name: Denoise
denoise.help: Learn a steady noise (fan, hiss, hum) while nothing else plays, then remove it.

speech-denoise.name: Speech Denoise
speech-denoise.help: Automatically reduce background noise around speech. Runs locally with a spectral method, not a machine-learning model.

spectral-gate.name: Spectral Gate
spectral-gate.help: Learn the noise at every frequency, then block whatever stays below it, like ReaFIR's gate. Shows a live spectrum.

fir-filter.name: FIR Filter
fir-filter.help: Give your sound the character of a room, speaker or mic from its impulse response (WAV or MP3, up to 2 s). Wet mix blends it with the original.

time-shift.name: Time Shift
time-shift.help: A DVR for live audio: pause, jump back or forward 10 s, and return to live. Keeps up to 120 s.

mixer.name: Mixer
mixer.help: Combine several sources into one, with a volume for each input.

duck.name: Duck
duck.help: Turn this audio down automatically while another source is loud (for example game sound while you talk), or in chosen Siege phases with Stats.cc. Choose the trigger in Properties.

input-switch.name: Input Switch
input-switch.help: Pass either input A or input B. Switching crossfades over 0.5 s (Shift-click for 2 s).

output-switch.name: Output Switch
output-switch.help: Send one signal to output A or B, such as headphones or OBS. Only the selected side receives audio; switch with Properties or Stream Deck.

recorder.name: Recorder
recorder.help: Record the sound passing through this point to a file on this PC.

mute.name: Mute
mute.help: Silence this part of the route without disconnecting anything.

meter.name: Meter
meter.help: Show the level of the sound at this point, to check it is neither too quiet nor clipping.

parametric-eq.name: Advanced EQ
parametric-eq.help: Place up to 16 EQ points with peaking, shelves, low/high/band pass, all pass, or notch filters.

compressor.name: Compressor
compressor.help: Even out loud and quiet moments so a voice sits at a steady level.

gate.name: Gate
gate.help: Silence quiet background noise between words; opens when you speak.

limiter.name: Limiter
limiter.help: Hold peaks under a ceiling so sudden loud sounds never clip or distort.

delay.name: Sync (delay)
delay.help: Delay audio by 0–1000 ms to line it up with video or another source. Chain several for longer delays.

graphic-eq.name: Graphic EQ
graphic-eq.help: Boost or cut ten fixed frequency bands, from deep bass (31.5 Hz) to air (16 kHz).

pitch.name: Pitch shift
pitch.help: Shift the pitch up or down without changing the speed.

fun-voice-changer.name: Fun Voice Changer
fun-voice-changer.help: Playful voice presets you can tweak: pitch correct, deep, chipmunk, robot, monster, radio, whisper and more. Adds 21 ms delay; output is mono.

common.availableInDesktop: Available in the AudioRouter desktop app.

topbar.openSessionTab: Open the Session tab to switch or manage sessions
topbar.saveTitleSaved: Saved route: changes survive restart and are included in exports
topbar.saveTitlePending: You have unsaved edits; save them to this session
topbar.saveTitleAuto: Parameter changes save automatically after a short pause
topbar.playTitle: Header Play starts the route; Stop stops the route. Source Play controls only that source and starts the route first if needed. Playing unsaved edits is a temporary preview and does not save them.

workbench.noSettingsMatch: No settings match. Ctrl+K searches everything.
workbench.statusProblem: Setup problems found. Open Status for details.

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.languageHint: AudioRouter switches language immediately. Device names, tool names and your own session names stay as they are.

updates.heading: New versions
updates.dailyCheck: Check GitHub once a day for a newer version
updates.privacyNote: Reads the public AudioRouter release list on github.com; nothing about you or your audio is sent. If GitHub cannot be reached, AudioRouter retries for up to 12 hours and then waits for the next day. It never downloads or installs an update; the release page opens in your browser. AudioRouter currently publishes prerelease builds.
updates.offDetail: Turn it on to look for new versions.
updates.idleDetail: Check now to look for a newer version.
updates.currentStable: No newer stable version was found.
updates.failedHeadline: Can't check for new versions right now.
updates.installedStableOnly: AudioRouter {{version}} is installed. Only stable releases are checked.
updates.offStored: No result is stored while checking is off.

devices.heading: Audio devices on this PC
devices.help: What Windows offers right now. To use one, add an Input Device or Output Device tool and choose it in that tool's Properties. AudioRouter never changes Windows defaults or volumes. Clear "Show in pickers" to keep a device you never use (a monitor's speakers, a webcam microphone) out of the device lists on this PC.
devices.inactive_one: {{count}} more device is unplugged or disabled in Windows.
devices.inactive_other: {{count}} more devices are unplugged or disabled in Windows.

native.noSession: No session to play. Open AudioRouter and create one.
native.playFailedConsent: Play failed: allow device access in the window first (press Play there once).
native.playFailedNoRoute: Play failed: no device route. Open AudioRouter and choose the devices.
native.autoplayPaused: Autoplay paused: unavailable saved sessions need recovery in AudioRouter.
native.autoplayFailed: Autoplay failed: the audio engine did not start
native.restorePaused: Restore paused: unavailable saved sessions need recovery.
native.restoredPartial: Restored {{restored}} of {{total}} routes after a restart
native.restoreFailed: Restore failed: the audio engine did not start

goalGuide.question: What do you want to do?
goalGuide.step1Recording: In Tools, add Application Capture and choose the exact running process in Properties. Capture includes its process tree, not a browser tab.
goalGuide.step1Voice: Use Set up for Discord to choose your exact microphone and paired voice cable and add optional voice cleanup.
goalGuide.step2Recording: Add a Recorder and connect only that application to it. Leave it unarmed until you deliberately choose to record.
goalGuide.step2Voice: Send only your processed microphone to the voice cable. Keep microphone monitoring muted; do not connect a headphone monitoring branch until you deliberately want it.
goalGuide.deviceHelp: check selected devices in Properties. An available device or running process does not prove audio is arriving.
goalGuide.signalHelp: review the route, then deliberately press Play. Make sound in the selected source and check fresh route meters. Silence needs investigation before continuing.
goalGuide.recordingVerifyHelp: deliberately arm and start the Recorder, stop it, then review the file for the selected app and absence of unrelated apps.
goalGuide.receivingVerifyHelp: open Discord or your receiving app, select the cable's recording end shown by setup, and use its input test. A closed app or correct device selection alone is not a successful audio test.
goalGuide.gamingNote: Keep game and browser audio out of the voice cable. Select headphones for Discord playback and check for duplicate playback separately.
goalGuide.footnote: This guide does not start audio, enable monitoring, arm recording, or change another app. The canvas remains available for advanced routes.

setupWorkbench.otherAppsHelp: AudioRouter does not change settings in Windows or in other apps. To send your processed microphone to Discord, OBS or a game, end the route in an Output Device set to a virtual cable (for example CABLE Input), then choose the matching input (CABLE Output) as the microphone in that app.

deviceTroubleshooting.bindingHelp: Devices chosen here are used only when a single route's Input Device or Output Device tool has no device of its own.

firstRun.heading: Set up a route on this PC
firstRun.connect: Connect to AudioRouter to check available devices.
firstRun.found_one: Found {{count}} input and {{renders}} {{outputs}}. Choose the exact devices in each tool's Properties.
firstRun.found_other: Found {{count}} inputs and {{renders}} {{outputs}}. Choose the exact devices in each tool's Properties.
firstRun.noPair: No complete input-and-output pair is available yet. Connect or enable your audio devices, then refresh this list. AudioRouter never installs audio drivers on its own.
firstRun.step1: Open Tools and add an Input Device and Output Device, or start with Test Signal.
firstRun.step2: Choose an available device in each tool's Properties, then connect the route.
firstRun.step3: Review the route and press Play when you are ready. AudioRouter never changes Windows default devices.
firstRun.virtualCable: To send your microphone to another app, use an existing supported virtual audio device such as VB-Cable or Voicemeeter. Install it separately from its vendor.

quit.unresponsiveMessage: Quit failed: AudioRouter's background service did not answer. Click Quit anyway to close it now. Audio stops, and a recording in progress is recovered the next time you open AudioRouter.
quit.refusedMessage: Quit refused: {{reason}}. Audio keeps playing; stop any recording and try again.
quit.anywayTitle: Close AudioRouter now without waiting for its background service. Recordings in progress are recovered next time.
quit.quitTitle: Stop audio, finish recordings and close AudioRouter (same as the tray's Quit). Unsaved edits come back next time you open it.

sessionSwitch.heading: Stop audio and switch session?
sessionSwitch.description: Switching stops all sessions listed below, including audio used by other apps. Their active recordings will stop and finalize; a finalization failure may leave recoverable partial files. The selected session stays stopped until you press Play.

startup.intro: Start with Windows in the tray (no window) and, if you like, play the selected session and start the API right away. Closing the window keeps audio playing in the tray.
startup.autoplayDescription: Plays the session selected here when AudioRouter starts, for example at sign-in. The tray menu's Play and Stop audio work the same way without opening this window.
startup.autoplayOn: AudioRouter will play the selected session when it starts.
startup.autoplayFailed: Autoplay could not be saved. Try again.
startup.apiHeading: Start the API when AudioRouter starts
startup.apiDescription: Keeps controllers such as a Stream Deck connected after a restart. The API uses the port and network it last started with (Settings, API), or this PC only on port 17891.
startup.apiOn: The API will start with AudioRouter.
startup.apiOff: Start the API from Settings, API, when you need it.
startup.apiFailed: API auto-start could not be saved. Try again.

flowAnimation.heading: Animated connections
flowAnimation.label: Travelling lights on connections
flowAnimation.onHelp: Lights travel along every connection that carries sound.
flowAnimation.focusHelp: The lights pause while you use another program (for example a game on another screen) and resume when you click back in. Colours, glow and meters keep updating.
flowAnimation.offHelp: No travelling lights. Colours, glow and meters still show the level. Uses the least CPU while this window is open.
flowAnimation.closing: Closing the window to the tray stops all drawing.

liveAutosave.heading: Live autosave
liveAutosave.label: Save parameter changes while audio plays
liveAutosave.onHelp: Changes to sliders and tool settings are saved automatically and applied to the playing audio. Changing the route still needs Save.
liveAutosave.offHelp: Parameter changes stay as an unsaved draft until you choose Save. Turning a tool on or off still applies immediately while audio plays.

deviceAccess.dialogTitle: Allow AudioRouter to use your audio devices?
deviceAccess.dialogDescription: To play this session, AudioRouter opens the microphones, speakers and virtual cables in it. It asks once on this computer. You can change this later under Settings → Device access.
deviceAccess.heading: Audio device access
deviceAccess.connectToCheck: Connect to the desktop backend to check audio device access.
deviceAccess.readFailed: Could not read audio device access. Use Check again.

troubleshoot.heading: Troubleshoot and recover
troubleshoot.manualHelp: You normally do not need this. Choose each device in the Input Device or Output Device tool's Properties and press Play. Use these controls to check a device's format, reopen a device after Windows reset it, run a deliberate VB-Cable loopback test, or add a loopback source.
troubleshoot.recoveryOwned: Recovery state is owned by the backend.

canvasKeyboard.connectHelp: The same as dragging from one tool to another on the canvas, for keyboard and screen-reader use.
